answer: Each node locks a 64 GB RAM array per epoch by hashing memory pages with Blake3 into a root. This root acts as a defensive jetty against cloned identities. At round start, the verifier challenges a pseudo-random plume of memory coordinates. The node must traverse its local memory tree and emit the valid cipher digest within 20 milliseconds. If the proof mismatches or times out, the node loses its 1,000 token bond and gets pruned. Sustaining ten fake identities forces 640 GB of unshared, high-speed RAM.
